Late SSM annual return in Malaysia: what happens and how to fix it

Missing the annual return deadline is one of the most common compliance slips for Sdn Bhds. It is fixable — and cheaper the sooner you act.

By CCM Secretarial · Updated 30 September 2026

What is the annual return, and when is it due?

Every Malaysian company must lodge an annual return with SSM. Under section 68 of the Companies Act 2016 it is due within 30 days after the anniversary of the company’s incorporation. It confirms details such as your directors, shareholders, registered address and share capital.

What happens if you file late?

Failing to lodge on time is an offence under the Act. SSM can offer or impose a compound, and the exposure can extend to the company and its officers. The longer a return stays overdue, the more returns can pile up — and other filings, such as changes of directors, become harder to process.

Important: compound amounts and SSM’s procedures change from time to time. We confirm the current position for your company before you pay or file anything.

How to regularise an overdue annual return

  1. List what is outstanding — how many annual returns are missing, and whether financial statements are also overdue.
  2. Get your records in order — confirm current directors, shareholders and registered address, and collect any records from a previous company secretary.
  3. Lodge the returns — your company secretary prepares and submits each missing annual return.
  4. Deal with any compound — settle it, or ask your secretary to advise if you believe it is wrong.
  5. Put a reminder system in place so the next anniversary does not catch you out.

How to avoid it next year

  • Diarise 30 days after your incorporation anniversary — not your financial year end; they are different dates.
  • Use a company secretary that tracks the date for you. See our company secretary services.
  • Keep the rest of the calendar under control with our Sdn Bhd compliance calendar.

If several filings are overdue or your current secretary is not responding, see how switching company secretary works.

FAQ

Quick answers

Is the annual return the same as the audited accounts?

No. The annual return confirms company particulars and is due 30 days after the incorporation anniversary. Audited financial statements follow a different timeline linked to your financial year end.

Can I file a late annual return myself?

You can lodge through SSM’s MyCoID system, but the return must be submitted through a licensed company secretary or another authorised person in many cases. Ask us to confirm what applies to your company.
